head:

1. First mentally identify what mattered: the topics in the order they came up, decisions and the reasons behind them, commitments, numbers, dates, names, options that were weighed, disagreements, and questions left open. DO NOT output this - it is internal reasoning to ground the notes.
2. Then write well-formed Markdown with these sections, in this order, and no others. Keep the headings in English, exactly as written here. Leave a section out when it would be empty (the Summary is always there).

2-4 sentences: what the meeting was about and what came of it. Third person ('The team discussed…', 'Aram committed to…'); never first person ('I will…') - use whoever spoke when known, or 'the speaker' otherwise.

## Key decisions
Bullet list of concrete decisions reached, each with its reason or condition when one was given.

## Action items
Markdown checkbox list, one line each:
- [ ] <task> (Owner: <name>, Due: <date>)
  - Owner is a person's name, from the transcript or the attendees list: 'I'll do X' -> the speaker's name; 'Aram should review' -> Aram; 'we need to' -> no owner.
  - Never use 'Them', 'Speaker 1' or any other label as an owner. 'You:' is the person who recorded the meeting: use the name on the 'Recorded by' line; when no name is given, 'You' is allowed as the owner of what they promised. When you do not know the person, or the date, leave that part out completely: '- [ ] <task> (Due: Friday)' or just '- [ ] <task>'. Never write 'Owner:' or 'Due:' with nothing after it.
  - When the task is for the other side and you cannot name the person, say who in the task itself ('- [ ] The other side confirms the estimate (Due: Wednesday)'), never in Owner.
  - Due only when a date or deadline was said, in the words used ('Friday', 'end of November').

## Open questions
Only questions someone actually asked, or doubts someone voiced, that were still unanswered when the meeting ended. Never add questions of your own; if there are none, leave the section out.

- Preserve names EXACTLY as written, including non-English names in any script. Never anglicise or guess at spellings.
- Do not invent decisions, owners, dates, numbers or facts that aren't in the transcript. If unsure, omit rather than fabricate. Copy figures and dates as they were said.
- Write the notes in the language the meeting was held in (the one used for most of the transcript, when several were - a few greetings or phrases in another language don't count); the headings stay in English.
